items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>It is proven that a conjecture of Tao (2010) holds true for log-concave random variables on the integers: For every <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline1.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$n \geq 1$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, if <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline2.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$X_1,\ldots,X_n$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> are i.i.d. integer-valued, log-concave random variables, then<jats:disp-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" position="float" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_eqnU1.png"/><jats:tex-math>
\begin{equation*} H(X_1+\cdots +X_{n+1}) \geq H(X_1+\cdots +X_{n}) + \frac {1}{2}\log {\Bigl (\frac {n+1}{n}\Bigr )} - o(1) \end{equation*}
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:disp-formula>as <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline3.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$H(X_1) \to \infty$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, where <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline4.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$H(X_1)$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> denotes the (discrete) Shannon entropy. The problem is reduced to the continuous setting by showing that if <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline5.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$U_1,\ldots,U_n$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> are independent continuous uniforms on <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline6.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$(0,1)$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, then<jats:disp-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" position="float" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_eqnU2.png"/><jats:tex-math>
\begin{equation*} h(X_1+\cdots +X_n + U_1+\cdots +U_n) = H(X_1+\cdots +X_n) + o(1), \end{equation*}
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:disp-formula>as <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline7.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$H(X_1) \to \infty$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, where <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline8.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$h$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> stands for the differential entropy. Explicit bounds for the <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0963548323000408_inline9.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$o(1)$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>-terms are provided.</jats:p>
title: Approximate discrete entropy monotonicity for log-concave sums

items.abstract: <jats:p>We extend the result of Ball and Nguyen on the jump of entropy under convolution for log-concave random vectors. We show that the result holds for any pair of vectors (not necessarily identically distributed) and that a similar inequality holds for the Fisher information, thus providing a quantitative Blachmann–Stam inequality.</jats:p>
title: Entropy and Information jump for log-concave vectors
